Diagnose whether entropy is associated with neighbourhood density

entropy_density_diagnostic.Rd

`entropy_density_diagnostic()` tests whether a per-cell entropy or plasticity score is associated with local neighbourhood density in an embedding. It is a diagnostic, not a correction: the returned residuals must not be interpreted as corrected entropy because a genuinely plastic biological state may itself occupy a diffuse region of the embedding.

Usage

entropy_density_diagnostic(
  seu,
  entropy,
  embedding,
  k = 30,
  group = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  log_density = FALSE,
  cluster_of_interest = NULL,
  plot_file = NULL
)

Arguments

seu

A Seurat object whose cells correspond, in the same order, to `entropy` and the rows of `embedding`. When `group` is supplied, it is looked up directly in this object's metadata.

entropy

Numeric vector with one entropy/plasticity value per cell.

embedding

Numeric matrix (cells by dimensions), in the same cell order as `entropy`.

k

Positive integer giving the number of nearest neighbours. Must be smaller than the number of cells. Default is 30.

group

Optional single character string naming a categorical column in `seu[[]]`. The function checks that the column exists before fitting the model. When supplied, residuals are summarized and plotted by that column.

covariates

Optional data frame or named list of numeric per-cell covariates. Each covariate is fitted alone and receives its own residual boxplot. Neighbourhood density is always included as a separate, independent model and is not added to the covariate models.

log_density

Logical; if `TRUE`, regress on `log(mean_knn_dist)`. The returned `mean_knn_dist` values remain on the original distance scale.

cluster_of_interest

Optional single group value to highlight in the boxplot. Ignored when `group` is `NULL`.

plot_file

Optional base file path for 300-dpi PNG output when `group` is supplied. Default `NULL` does not save. With multiple covariates, the covariate name is appended to create one file per plot.

Value

A list with per-cell `mean_knn_dist`; a residual data frame with one column per separate model; the global Spearman `correlation`; named `regressions`; an optional combined `group_summary`; an optional Spearman `covariate_correlations` matrix; named `plots`; and optional named `plot_files`. Residuals are diagnostic values, not corrected scores.

Details

Local sparsity is measured as the mean distance to each cell's `k` nearest neighbours (excluding the cell itself). Larger values therefore mean a sparser neighbourhood. The function reports the global Spearman correlation between entropy and this distance. It always fits density as its own model (`entropy ~ density`). Every supplied covariate is then fitted in a completely independent model (`entropy ~ covariate`): covariates are never combined with density or with one another. Positive residuals indicate entropy above the relevant fitted trend; negative residuals indicate entropy below it.

Use the same embedding and `k` that were used to calculate entropy whenever possible. The diagnostic is modality-agnostic and can be used with any numeric cell embedding.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
embedding <- Seurat::Embeddings(seu[["pca"]])
result <- entropy_density_diagnostic(
  seu = seu, entropy = seu$entropy_mean_RNA, embedding = embedding,
  k = 15, group = "celltype",
  plot_file = NULL
)
result$correlation
result$group_summary
} # }
